3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: I was travelling to the snow-covered city of Narbel in the Nargis region for the rural development forum organized by the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Education.

4.speaker: Serge Wolkner
4.text: “We will be arriving at Hotel West in a few minutes, sir.”

5.speaker: Player
5.text: “Can't say it's been a comfortable ride, Serge.”

8.speaker: Serge Wolkner
8.text: “I am sorry sir. The roads here aren't the best.”

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: After a moment, Serge started to smile under his moustache.

11.speaker: Serge Wolkner
11.text: “Sir, I just want to say... It has been great these last two months.”

12.speaker: Serge Wolkner
12.text: “As you know, my wife Suzan recently gave birth to our son. And now my daughter just started at a very good high school in Holsord."

14.speaker: Player
14.text: “Get ready, Serge. Because life is about to become a lot busier.”

15.speaker: Serge Wolkner
15.text: “The doctors said he is very healthy and thankfully so is my wife.”

16.speaker: Serge Wolkner
16.text: “But I shouldn't have made my insecurity get to me. Erica outsmarts me all the time. I'm very proud to have a daughter like her.”

17.speaker: Serge Wolkner
17.text: “How are your children, sir, if I may ask?”

18.speaker: Player
18.text: “Tell me more about Suzan. What kind of a person is she?”

20.speaker: Player
20.text: “Deana is as lively as ever, but Franc seems to be a little distant.”

21.speaker: Player
21.text: “They are both doing just fine. Going through different phases in life.”

22.speaker: Player
22.text: “So that means she must have gotten the smarts from her mother.”

23.speaker: Player
23.text: “I also hope that Deana will grow to be like her mother someday.”

24.speaker: Serge Wolkner
24.text: “Have I told you, sir? We named my son Georg.”

25.speaker: Serge Wolkner
25.text: “Oh, I know, sir. It already is very busy. My daughter is a handful.”

26.speaker: Serge Wolkner
26.text: “I appreciate it, sir. Truly. I was worried that I wouldn't be able to afford a good private school if she scored less in the entrance exams.”

27.speaker: Serge Wolkner
27.text: “I come from a big family. I'm one of five siblings so having company is a constant in my life.”

28.speaker: Serge Wolkner
28.text: “She's beautiful, of course. But what I really admire is her selflessness.”

30.speaker: Serge Wolkner
30.text: “That's very normal, sir. He is at that age. All of us went through a rebellious phase.”

31.speaker: Narrator
31.text: The motorcade began approaching the hotel.

32.speaker: Serge Wolkner
32.text: “I'm sure she will sir. After all she is the daughter of a lion and a lioness.”

40.speaker: Player
40.text: “That's good. I hope the hospital had a good service.”

41.speaker: Serge Wolkner
41.text: “Normally, we would have been treated in one of the suburban hospitals.”

42.speaker: Serge Wolkner
42.text: “But thanks to the special coverage of the presidential staff, we were transferred to Emerald State Hospital.”

44.speaker: Player
44.text: “We need to increase the quality of the services for all.”

46.speaker: Serge Wolkner
46.text: “You could call it a little traditional but it just feels right.”

48.speaker: Player
48.text: “Selflessness is a respectable trait to have.”

49.speaker: Player
49.text: “Monica is persevering. It can be inspiring at times to have a partner like that.”

51.speaker: Player
51.text: “This is unacceptable. We need to invest in infrastructure here.”

52.speaker: Player
52.text: “I do not value insecurity in my employees, Serge.”

53.speaker: Serge Wolkner
53.text: “Yes, sir. I will be more careful from now on.”

54.speaker: Serge Wolkner
54.text: “She is an inspiration for almost all women in the country.”

56.speaker: Player
56.text: “Enough talking, Serge. Focus on the road.”

57.speaker: Serge Wolkner
57.text: “The bazaar there is quite unique and it is a good city. Nothing compares to Holsord of course.”

58.speaker: Serge Wolkner
58.text: “It should be mutual, that is what matters most.”

59.speaker: Serge Wolkner
59.text: “It's only fitting. A lioness for a lion.”

60.speaker: Serge Wolkner
60.text: “The equipment and the staff were exceptional.”

61.speaker: Serge Wolkner
61.text: “There are far more unfortunate people in this country. But thanks.”

62.speaker: Serge Wolkner
62.text: “That sounds like a tough issue to solve.”

63.speaker: Serge Wolkner
63.text: “I'm sorry. I will drive more carefully, sir.”

64.speaker: Serge Wolkner
64.text: “I agree sir. We still need to drive back tomorrow unless you use one of those new helicopters.”

65.speaker: Serge Wolkner
65.text: “Yes sir. I hope the car is fine too.”

72.speaker: Narrator
72.text: The scenery so far, however, was a reflection of Narbel's neglect. The main roads to the city were not maintained well. There were many bumps and empty discolored spots in the asphalt.

73.speaker: Narrator
73.text: The scenery so far, however, was a reflection of Narbel's neglect. The main roads to the city were not maintained well. There were many bumps and empty discolored spots in the asphalt.

75.speaker: Player
75.text: “I expect so much from them. They will make me proud.”

76.speaker: Serge Wolkner
76.text: “It must not be easy to be the children of a high-profile person like you.”

77.speaker: Serge Wolkner
77.text: “My daughter looks up to the First Lady for inspiration and it's not just limited to my daughter, sir.”

78.speaker: Serge Wolkner
78.text: “It must be sir. We sometimes forget the important people in life between all the responsibility and rush.”

80.speaker: Serge Wolkner
80.text: “I had some troubles communicating with Erica as she grew up, but we found a common ground by going to plays.”

81.speaker: Player
81.text: “My children can talk to me if they want. It is up to them.”

83.speaker: Serge Wolkner
83.text: “...I was unlucky. I never had a connection with my father. He was absent from our life, and I just can't have the same situation with my children...”

85.speaker: Player
85.text: “Traditional or not if it is what you want, that is all that matters.”

88.speaker: Serge Wolkner
88.text: “Yes and it depends on what type of environment it is. If its hostile...”

89.speaker: Serge Wolkner
89.text: “We keep forgetting what we want and lose ourselves in the process.”

91.speaker: Serge Wolkner
91.text: “She has a good heart. Her family comes from Sarna, so they are a little more traditional.”

92.speaker: Narrator
92.text: The mountainous city was infamously one of Sordland's poorest. It had a gritty edge, and its people were hardy and wary.

93.speaker: Narrator
93.text: Even after the discovery of gas and oil in the area, years of neglect by the central government were apparent on the buildings and the general infrastructure. The natural resources were now under the control of Gasom, which elevated the corporation to a place of power.

94.speaker: Narrator
94.text: My task in this forum was mainly symbolic. Fake smiles and handshakes with oil barons, meeting with local politicians, but most importantly of all, making sure that Narbel did not feel like it was forgotten by the government.

95.speaker: Narrator
95.text: As if my discomfort from the bumpy ride was apparent to him, Serge rolled down the partition window.

96.speaker: Player
96.text: “Good. Whatever gets us out of here quickly.”

97.speaker: Narrator
97.text: I let out a deep sigh.

99.speaker: Serge Wolkner
99.text: “Thankfully, my work times allow me to spend some time with my family, except for these distant trips. I'm very lucky to have this job.”

100.speaker: Narrator
100.text: Serge continued after a moment of silence.

101.speaker: Narrator
101.text: Navigating and swerving to avoid the inconveniences, our motorcade finally started nearing the city.

102.speaker: Player
102.text: “They are fine, but that's not your business Serge.”

104.speaker: Narrator
104.text: He looked visibly irked by my comment and nodded.

105.speaker: Player
105.text: “I expect you to do your job. Not ask questions about my private life.”

108.speaker: Narrator
108.text: There was a long silence. After several minutes, Serge attempted to break silence.

109.speaker: Narrator
109.text: There was a long silence. After several minutes, Serge attempted to break silence.

113.speaker: Player
113.text: “Spare me your lectures about parenthood, Serge.”

117.speaker: Narrator
117.text: My thoughts faded to my childhood. My father was also absent from home most of the time. I never connected with him, just like Serge.

118.speaker: Narrator
118.text: Being a president meant that I had to be away from home most of the time.

119.speaker: Narrator
119.text: I wondered if Franc also thought of me as an absent father figure. Could that be the reason behind his attitude?

120.speaker: Serge Wolkner
120.text: “But at the same time, it must be hard for the First Lady as well.”

122.speaker: Player
122.text: “You are right. It is hard for her.”

123.speaker: Player
123.text: “It is hard for both of us.”

124.speaker: Serge Wolkner
124.text: “My daughter looks up to the First Lady for inspiration. Not only my daughter, sir."

125.speaker: Serge Wolkner
125.text: “All this attention, adjusting to this new high-profile life, and a husband that has great responsibility...”

126.speaker: Player
126.text: “Very good. I must tend to my documents for a bit.”

128.speaker: Narrator
128.text: The Hotel West was supposedly the best hotel in Narbel. The large 25-story main building was undoubtedly one of the taller and more expensive buildings in the city. It towered over the nearby slums and had been a target for protests when it was first built.

129.speaker: Narrator
129.text: A crowd was gathered in front of the hotel with the welcoming committee at its centre. As we approached the red carpeted entrance I could see the Mayor of Narbel and his top aides.

130.speaker: Narrator
130.text: Serge got out of the car and opened the door. He bowed his head respectfully and gestured towards the entrance.

133.speaker: Narrator
133.text: As soon as I left the vehicle, the fresh air of Narbel filled my lungs.

134.speaker: Narrator
134.text: Almost immediately, everyone present in the crowd flocked over to me with an excessive display of courtesy, smiles and handshakes while I donned the mask of a politician.

135.speaker: Narrator
135.text: A mask that I was very used to.

139.speaker: Narrator
139.text: The car hit a major pothole and a bump which lifted us up in our seats for a second.

140.speaker: Serge Wolkner
140.text: “I've already started thinking about their university education. Especially Erica.”

141.speaker: Serge Wolkner
141.text: “I want to send her to a good private school but with the current state of the economy, it's going to be hard for us.”

142.speaker: Player
142.text: “We will fix the economy. One way or another.”

143.speaker: Player
143.text: “You know what? I can support the education of your children." [-1 Personal Wealth]

145.speaker: Serge Wolkner
145.text: “Mr. President, there is no way I can--.”

146.speaker: Narrator
146.text: With one look from me, Serge cut his sentence short and nodded at me after removing his hat.

147.speaker: Serge Wolkner
147.text: “Mr. President, I don't know how I can ever repay you for this.”

150.speaker: Serge Wolkner
150.text: “If anyone can, that's you, Mr. President.”

151.speaker: Serge Wolkner
151.text: “If anyone can fix the economy, that's you, Mr. President.”

152.speaker: Player
152.text: “A good education is more valuable than any amount of money.”

153.speaker: Player
153.text: “I hope you return the favor by helping someone in need someday. Just like I did.”

157.speaker: Serge Wolkner
157.text: “I think I have decided. I will give your name to my boy. ”

160.speaker: Player
160.text: “It has a nice ring to it. I like it.”

183.speaker: Narrator
183.text: The scenery so far, however, was a reflection of Narbel's neglect. The main roads to the city were not maintained well. There were many bumps and empty discolored spots in the asphalt.

184.speaker: Player
184.text: “That's great news, Serge. I'm happy for you.”

188.speaker: Player
188.text: “Let's not talk about my family, Serge.”

198.speaker: Player
198.text: “My driver's family shouldn't want for anything in this world. I'll cover your children's education and any other extra expenses you need." [-2 Personal Wealth]
